lead.headline: Trump-Linked World Liberty Financial Wins OCC Trust Charter as SEC Cancels Crypto Rulemaking Session
lead.tldr: Regulatory momentum in U.S. crypto is splitting along political fault lines: conditional federal banking approval for a Trump-affiliated entity contrasts with procedural gridlock at the SEC, where the CLARITY Act's stall killed a key rulemaking meeting. For investors underwriting U.S. policy risk, the signal is institutional capture, not regulatory clarity.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, here is what moved in Web3 over the last 24 hours and why the U.S. regulatory picture is fragmenting into something more tactical than coherent.

top_signals.title: Wallet provider SafePal says data breach exposed personal info of nearly 40,000 customers
top_signals.summary: Wallet provider SafePal has confirmed a data breach that exposed the personal information of approximately 40,000 customers. While the company recently identified the root cause, users had reported phishing attempts linked to the breach as early as July.
top_signals.why_it_matters: SafePal's breach of 40,000 customer records, with phishing attempts predating disclosure by months, exposes the operational gap between incident detection and user notification that liability frameworks have yet to close.

top_signals.title: OCC grants conditional approval for Trump-backed World Liberty National Trust bank
top_signals.summary: World Liberty Financial, a project backed by Donald Trump, has received preliminary approval from the OCC to operate as a national trust bank. This move signals a significant regulatory step for the project's integration into the traditional banking system.
top_signals.why_it_matters: OCC conditional approval for World Liberty Financial's national trust charter represents a politicalized regulatory precedent: a project tied to a presidential candidate now holds a federal banking credential that most crypto-native firms have failed to secure.

top_signals.title: Ethereum devs to narrow 66 proposals tied to Hegotá upgrade5m, Ethereum devs to narrow 66 proposals tied to Hegotá upgradeThe Hegotá upgrade aims to introduce more native privacy for Ethereum applications.
top_signals.summary: Ethereum developers are working to refine and narrow down 66 proposals associated with the upcoming Hegotá upgrade. The primary goal of this upgrade is to integrate more native privacy features for applications building on the network.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Ethereum's Hegotá upgrade, narrowing 66 proposals toward native privacy primitives, tests whether L1 privacy can become a competitive moat against L2s and alternative chains that have captured that narrative.

top_signals.title: SEC cancels key crypto regulatory meeting10m, SEC cancels key crypto regulatory meetingThe SEC canceled a meeting on proposed crypto offering rules after the Senate left for recess without voting on the CLARITY Act.
top_signals.summary: The SEC has canceled a meeting regarding proposed crypto offering rules. This decision follows the Senate's departure for recess without a vote on the CLARITY Act.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The SEC's cancellation of its crypto offering rules meeting after Senate recess killed CLARITY Act momentum reveals how dependent U.S. regulatory development is on legislative sequencing—creating timing risk for any firm building around proposed safe harbors.

top_signals.title: Chainalysis sues US over $95M ICE contract with TRM Labs
top_signals.summary: Chainalysis has filed a lawsuit against the US government regarding a $95 million contract awarded to TRM Labs by ICE. TRM Labs has intervened in the procurement dispute, with court arguments scheduled for September.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Chainalysis's lawsuit over ICE's $95 million TRM Labs contract signals intensifying competition in government blockchain analytics procurement, where incumbency advantages in classified workflows are now being contested in open court.

on_the_radar.title: JPMorgan cut Polymarket’s banking ties in October but still wants a role in a potential IPO: FT
on_the_radar.summary: JPMorgan severed its banking ties with prediction market Polymarket in October, though the bank reportedly remains interested in a potential future IPO. Polymarket has since transitioned its accounts to an unidentified lender while maintaining a relationship with JPMorgan.

on_the_radar.summary: Payward, the parent company of Kraken, reported a 17% increase in revenue despite a decline in trading volume during the second quarter. The financial results highlight a divergence between top-line growth and active trading activity.

linkedin_post:
The OCC handed a conditional national trust charter to World Liberty Financial this week. Same week, the SEC canceled its crypto rulemaking session because the Senate left town without touching the CLARITY Act. These are not two data points about 'regulatory momentum.' They are one data point about regulatory arbitrage by political proximity.

We have never seen a project this explicitly tied to a presidential candidate secure federal banking infrastructure while the agency that actually writes crypto enforcement policy goes dark for procedural reasons. The market is pricing this as bullish for DeFi integration into traditional rails. We underwrite it differently: this is a single-firm subsidy, not a sectoral opening. The value is shifting toward entities that can navigate OCC consent orders and away from anyone waiting for SEC rulemaking to clarify token issuance.

What would change our view? A second non-politicalized crypto trust charter approved on similar timelines. Without that, this reads as contingent access, not competitive advantage. The test is whether World Liberty can convert conditional approval into an operational balance sheet before the political cycle turns.

SafePal's breach—40,000 records, phishing in July, disclosure now—runs on a parallel track. Hardware wallet providers are still underwriting user data risk as if the product were only key management. It isn't. The liability model hasn't caught up.

We are watching who else applies for OCC trust status, and whether any of them move this fast.
